candidates.title: Prepare booking event notices for review

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare booking confirmation and provider assignment notices from a test booking record, with payment state and customer alert as separate fields.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can n8n help automate booking confirmations, provider assignment notifications, payment status updates, and customer alerts?

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable set of booking and provider notification drafts from one synthetic booking record.
inputs: Synthetic booking ID and service type
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters a synthetic booking or starts a test run.
steps: Validate required fields and reject incomplete test records.
Select a template for booking confirmation and provider assignment.
Draft separate customer and provider messages.
Mark payment status as supplied input without attempting payment processing.
Show all drafts for operator review and record approval in a test log.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed synthetic booking, check that the right two drafts contain the matching booking ID and supplied status, with no invented fields.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies fictional records, verifies assignments and payment state, and approves every message; no real customer or payment data is needed.
unverified: n8n node and API capabilities for this exact flow
External endpoint behavior and payment persistence
Whether operators repeat this chore or would pay for a tool

ease.reason: A student can mock a booking record and draft notices, but no supplied implementation reference supports these integrations.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small on-demand service operators may pay for setup; the request establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week prototype can generate reviewable notices from synthetic bookings; live APIs and payment persistence remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed event-to-draft loop can repeat, but an operator must verify assignment and payment state and approve messages.

evidence.reason: The post names bookings, provider assignment, payment updates and customer alerts, but gives no frequency or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a proposed bounded experiment; provisional mean is below 6. The source establishes the chore only, not a working AI service or paying customer.

candidates.title: Flag webhook record update mismatches

demandEvidence.chore: Create a review checklist for webhook events that arrive but do not update the intended record.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Webhooks receiving data but not updating the correct records

experimentPlan.output: A short mismatch report comparing a supplied webhook example with its expected synthetic record.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a sample event and expected record for review.
steps: Read the expected key and mapped fields supplied by the operator.
Compare those fields with the synthetic event and prior record.
Flag missing values or mismatches without proposing live edits.
If the event is marked as failed, add a note that Make error handlers can route module errors.
Produce a checklist for an operator to verify in a test scenario.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a small set of fixed synthetic payloads, report every deliberately missing or mismatched key and no other fields.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: An operator supplies test payloads and mapping expectations, checks any diagnosis, and applies changes manually after permission and privacy review.
unverified: Whether Make can expose the needed payload and mapping details
Actual cause of any reported production mismatch
Support for record lookup, deduplication, retries or safe repairs

ease.reason: A beginner can test a checklist on synthetic webhook and record pairs; Make documentation supports error handling routes, not record matching.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: automation consultants may pay for faster troubleshooting; the post establishes no independent buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare supplied fields; Make documents error routes that keep scenarios running, but not record matching or live connections.

autonomy.reason: The checker could flag differences in a proposed mock; no source supports this automation, and an operator must diagnose and change the workflow.

evidence.reason: The full post lists webhook updates and wrong records among small fixes, then offers fixed-price help; frequency is not established.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a proposed bounded experiment; provisional mean is below 6. The source establishes the chore only, not a working AI service or paying customer.

candidates.title: Compare AWS scaling options from test inputs

demandEvidence.chore: Draft a comparison memo from operator supplied workload and cost examples.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: If you are a bootstrapped startup and need to scale on AWS but can't afford it

experimentPlan.output: A comparison memo organizing supplied workload goals and cost options for human review.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters a fictional scaling question and candidate options.
steps: Check that each option has a supplied cost and configuration label.
Group options by the operator supplied workload goal.
Draft a plain language comparison using only entered facts.
Flag missing costs and assumptions instead of filling them in.
Return a memo with a human verification checklist.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed synthetic example, verify every displayed cost and configuration matches the inputs and missing values are flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A qualified operator validates AWS pricing and architecture and authorizes any real change; the prototype uses fictional inputs only.
unverified: Current AWS pricing and workload suitability
Access to verified architecture and cost information
Whether a customer would pay for this proposed memo

ease.reason: A beginner can organize fictional cost and workload inputs, but the post supplies no AWS implementation or cost reference.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: bootstrapped startups may pay for affordable scaling advice; the post offers help but proves no AI service buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can format operator supplied options; accurate AWS recommendations and live account analysis remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A tool could format inputs and draft comparisons, but an operator must validate costs and approve every infrastructure change.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly offers AWS scaling help to bootstrapped startups, but gives no repeated task, workload details or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a proposed bounded experiment; provisional mean is below 6. The source establishes the chore only, not a working AI service or paying customer.
